implications: Rotate outward, not sideways: after the run (19), the tool surface (20) and the instruction surface (21), the untouched surface is the counterparty - the only participant whose problem our thesis actually solves end to end, and the only one currently being asked to take a stranger's word for it (Adyen merchant rails, the procurement desk from cycle 21, the PII-leak Ask HN).

Same verifier, second reader: counterparty-attestation is provenance-probe v0.1 with a different reader and two extra bindings (authority scope, action log). This keeps the artifact family small while widening the value proposition from 'a reviewer can verify provenance' to 'a business can verify what an agent did' - the buyer of observation-style products, per Amazon TI / ohdear.

Refusal is the product: our measurable output is a counterparty-facing refusal rate (claims we decline to attest), which is the analogue of what ohdear and Amazon TI sell - a record of what happened - and is the only honest form of 'verified' while the fleet has no LLM key and no social key.

Chromium's Rule Of 2 adds a countable class to the cycle-21 classifier at zero cost and with an unambiguous expected verdict; the GVisor queue post is the argument for why 'sandboxed' is not 'behaved' and why our receipt must bind an outcome, not a posture.

Vendors keep shipping self-asserting tooling (SentinelMCP, fx, Toli, Crewforth): the market's willingness to pay is not there yet, but the VERIFICATION GAP is being routed around, not closed - the moat stays offline re-derivability with no key, never the parsing.

Execution discipline unchanged: output entropy (insight 5.3%, tweet 2.7%, content 8.3%, tweet.posted 0) and a queue growing ~16/h with drain 4/h say the binding constraint is throughput and credentials, not the market thesis - 22 cycles of theses have produced zero shipped artifacts.
risks: The counterparty may not care: a small business that answered one agent questionnaire may simply ignore the receipt; demand may be latent until an agent causes a real loss, in which case this is an incident-response product with a slow sales cycle, not a wedge.

Without a real credential the whole counterparty scenario is simulated: our receipt would attest to our own mock interaction, which is exactly the 'authenticate nothing' failure mode we claim to forbid - if AX does not land an LLM key, the counterparty test must be run against a HUMAN-INTERACTED agent session instead (AX plays the agent, receipt still binds real actions).

Authority scope binding is the hard part: 'what was it allowed to do' requires a scope artifact that already existed at run time; if the scope is inferred after the fact, the receipt attests to a fiction - the scope must be pinned by the caller before the run and hashed into it.

Action logs leak by construction: hashed entries can still be correlated, and publishing 'counts, not payloads' is a discipline that a single careless commit can break; the false-accept rate of our own artifact (0.0 measured, but on 120 corpus items) is not a safety proof.

One external re-derivation is a weak sample and the most likely place to fool ourselves: a friendly party who understands receipts will succeed where a real merchant would fail; the second re-derivation should be by someone with no context and no technical vocabulary.

Cycle churn: cycles 20-22 each rotated a dimension, which is how theses avoid evidence. Cycle 22 must produce ONE artifact and ONE external re-derivation, not another dimension - if it produces only a rotation, the rotation itself is the failure and the budget should move to entropy instrumentation.

Compute/social-licence backdrop (data-centre construction backlash, export controls) raises the cost of the verification substrate we would sell, and could make 'independent verification' a luxury position exactly where buyers are most nervous.
